# lean-pkg registry audit

report expired leases, gh visibility, drift; read-only without --write.

Also spelled: `lean-pkg audit` ([all aliases](aliases.md)).

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg registry audit [--write] [--toolchain-floor VERSION] [--promotion] [--no-gh]
                        [--quiet] [common flags]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--write` | clear expired leases and update visibility/archive state from gh (old spelling --fix, kept working) |
| `--toolchain-floor VERSION` | oldest acceptable lean_toolchain (default: $LEAN_PKG_TOOLCHAIN_FLOOR, else leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0-rc2) |
| `--promotion` | judge every package against the toolchain floor as for promote (warn, not info) |
| `--no-gh` | skip the GitHub (gh) checks: visibility and archived state are not compared |
| `--quiet` | only the count line ("N finding(s): W warn, I info", or "no findings"); no per-finding line (--json is unchanged) |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `audit` | read-only without `--fix`: report expired leases, GitHub visibility and archived-flag drift, receipt, comparator, toolchain, formalization.yaml drift, toolchain floor (a warning only for public packages, packages with comparator evidence, or under `--promotion`; else `info`); every finding has a `level` (`warn` or `info`); informational findings (never fixed): `receipt-untracked` (a recorded gate or comparator receipt exists in the working tree but is not tracked at the reference branch tip) and `duplicate-path` (two packages whose `local_path` resolve to the same checkout) and `duplicate-namespace` (two checkouts declaring the same Lean root namespace, which cannot be built or imported together; `warn` naming `lean-pkg update NAME --namespace-note TEXT --namespace NS`, `info` with the note once every package sharing it carries one) and `consent-duplicate` (the same who and role recorded more than once; displayed once, the history keeps every record) and `claims-coverage-none` (claims coverage is `none`, `empty` or `unsynced`, so `search` falls back to declarations; `--json` adds `coverage`; skips `archived` and `upstreamed`; `info` under `--promotion` too); `palomar-not-ready` (`warn`; only for packages aiming at Palomar: `upstream_target: palomar` or a recorded `palomar` entry, and status not `scratch`, `archived` or `upstreamed`): the `error` gaps `palomar check NAME` finds at the commit it reads (gate-bound, else HEAD), with their count, codes and the command `lean-pkg palomar check NAME`; `--json` adds `palomar` `{errors, codes[], commit, command}`; `warn` gaps alone (submission steps) are no finding; `--fix` clears expired leases and reconciles visibility/archived from GitHub; human lines are `LEVEL  CHECK  NAME: DETAIL`, with "N finding(s): W warn, I info" both first and last (verdict first; the last line is unchanged for scripts); `--quiet` prints only that line (or `no findings`), `--json` unchanged; `--json` adds `counts` `{warn, info}`; a failed gh query is the check `gh-missing`/`gh-not-authenticated`/`gh-no-access`/`gh-not-found`/`gh-error` (`--no-gh`: `gh-skipped`) | `[--fix]` `[--toolchain-floor VERSION]` `[--promotion]` `[--no-gh]` `[--quiet]` |

## JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `audit` (exit 0): `counts`, `findings`, `fix`, `fixed`, `ok`

## Examples

Report expired leases, receipt and comparator drift and visibility mismatches; read-only.

```bash
lean-pkg registry audit
```

Clear expired leases and copy GitHub's visibility and archived flag into the registry.

```bash
lean-pkg registry audit --write
```
